_note: Rover test planner (hand-written config, read by app/src/rover.js). Each part = the card variables it depends on + the margin (±) it tolerates. margin null = the tolerance of configs/variables.yaml. All margins and caps are chosen by the team: change them here, the app recomputes.

rules.field: at least one Earth search cell has EVERY variable of the part within ± margin of the target cell
rules.partial: only within ± 2 × margin, or a variable is missing, or physics caps it (gravity, thin air)
rules.lab: no Earth cell even within ± 2 × margin, or the part needs vacuum

parts.name: Wheels & suspension

mars.why: Mars gravity is 0.38 g: at full Earth weight the wheels sink and slip differently. NASA drives a stripped-down 'Scarecrow' rover that weighs on Earth what the real one weighs on Mars.

moon.why: Lunar gravity is 0.17 g: at full Earth weight the wheels sink and slip differently, so the field test needs a lightened rover.

parts.story: Spirit got stuck in soft sand in 2009 and never drove again. Curiosity's wheels were punctured by sharp rocks.
parts.lab: lightened test rover or a weight off-loading rig

parts.name: Mast cameras & navigation

moon.why: No air on the Moon: shadows are pitch black and there is no sky glow. Earth's atmosphere always softens them.

story.mars: The rover drives itself from its stereo cameras: the height of the Sun decides how long the shadows are and what the cameras can see.
story.moon: Near the lunar poles the Sun never climbs more than a few degrees above the horizon: shadows are kilometres long and hide the hazards.

parts.lab: dark hall with a single low lamp (lighting test bed)

parts.name: Robotic arm & coring drill

moon.why: Vacuum: there is no air to cool the bit or to carry the cuttings away.

parts.story: Perseverance's first core (August 2021) came up empty: the rock crumbled to powder inside the tube.
parts.lab: cold vacuum chamber with frozen regolith simulant

moon.why: Vacuum: heat leaves only by radiation. In Earth's air, convection changes the whole heat balance.

mars.why: Mars air has about 0.6 % of Earth's pressure: far less convective cooling than at any Earth field site.

story.mars: Mars nights fall below -80 °C: heaters and the waste heat of the power source keep the electronics alive until morning.
story.moon: India's Pragyan rover never woke up after its first lunar night (2023).

moon.why: The Moon has no airborne dust: its dust is sharp, electrically charged and clings in vacuum. No field site on Earth reproduces it.

story.mars: The 2018 global dust storm ended Opportunity's mission. Dust also coats optics and creeps into joints.
story.moon: Apollo crews found lunar dust everywhere: it jammed joints, scratched visors and wore through the outer layers of their suits.
